title: The Beach Blanket Review
dek: Twelve photographed blankets, seven group systems, one exact $99.99 sand kit, and zero invented affiliate codes
body:
Beach Commons V8 compares twelve current blankets by the jobs their materials can actually do: floor, softness, warmth, sand behavior, packability, anchoring, care, and social visibility. Each review uses a reduced, credited product photograph from the maker or merchant as an editorial reference—not PointCast product photography or proof of hands-on testing.

The useful argument is that one blanket rarely does every job well. CGear's six-foot sand-through mat and Matador's pocket blanket make an exact $99.99 pair before tax. One $39.99 IKEA SOLUPPGÅNG picnic blanket and three $19.99 washable throws make a $99.96 color field. A Nomadix water-resistant base and oversized Kelty insulated blanket make a $124.90 sunset stack. Seven computed systems publish the product mix, total, group size, and a human carry-and-wash assignment.

Every shopping link is plain. PointCast earns $0 and has no enrolled merchant affiliate ID, creator code, referral parameter, sponsored placement, or supplied product sample in this edition. The affiliate ledger instead publishes official application paths for Kelty, Slowtide, Nomadix, Rumpl, Business & Pleasure Co., and REI. Merchant signup offers are labeled as merchant offers and dated; they are not PointCast codes.

The field arrangement is an archipelago rather than a carpet: small rooms with visible sand lanes for circulation, access, and teardown. Blankets stay outside the ember and fire-steward zone. Beach Commons remains unofficial and unpermitted; current LA County visitor, access, and rules pages control any real use of Dockweiler.
